addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

    )

    IF (@MFLAG = 'OCR_ENABLED_COUNT')
    BEGIN

        INSERT INTO @TEMP_OCR_FEATURE
        SELECT
            @serverName,

                WHERE T2.COMPANY_LICENSE = T.COMPANY_LICENSE
                  AND T2.FEATURES = T.FEATURES

        GROUP BY
            T.COMPANY_LICENSE,
            CM.CLIENT_NAME,
            T.FEATURES,
            CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), T.ACTIVEON, 105),
            CASE WHEN CONVERT(DATE, T.INACTIVEON) = '1900-01-01' THEN ''
                 ELSE CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), T.INACTIVEON, 105) END;

        -- Get latest DB connection details for each OCR company
        INSERT INTO @TEMP_DATABASE_DETAILS
        SELECT

            d.SERVER_NAME,

using ClosedXML.Excel;

namespace DSRAutoMailScheduler
{
    class Program
    {
        private static readonly Logger Logger = LogManager.GetCurrentClassLogger();
        private static SmtpSettings _smtpSettings;
        private static Dictionary<string, string> _serverDict;
        private static string ReportFolder;
        private static string fileName;
        private static string savePath;

        public class SmtpSettings
        {
            public string Mail_header { get; set; }
            public string Host { get; set; }
            public string username { get; set; }
            public string password { get; set; }
            public int SmtpPort { get; set; }
            public bool enableSsl { get; set; }
            public string FromEmail { get; set; }
            public string[] ToEmails { get; set; }
            public string[] CCEmails { get; set; }
            public string Subject { get; set; }
            public string Body { get; set; }
        }

        public class RowPointers
        {
            public int ClientRow  = 1;   // Sheet 1: OCR_AI ENABLED CLIENT LIST
            public int JobRow     = 1;   // Sheet 2: OCR_AI TOTAL JOB COUNT
            public int FormatRow  = 1;   // Sheet 3: OCR_AI Total Format details
        }

        static async Task Main(string[] args)
        {
            try
            {
                RowPointers rows = new RowPointers();

                var builder = new ConfigurationBuilder()
                    .SetBasePath(AppContext.BaseDirectory)
                    .AddJsonFile("appsettings.json", optional: false, reloadOnChange: true);

                IConfiguration config = builder.Build();
                _smtpSettings  = config.GetSection("SmtpSettings").Get<SmtpSettings>();
                _serverDict    = config.GetSection("server_ip_list").Get<Dictionary<string, string>>();
                ReportFolder   = config.GetSection("ReportSettings:ReportFolder").Value;

                if (!Directory.Exists(ReportFolder))
                    Directory.CreateDirectory(ReportFolder);

                using var workbook = new XLWorkbook();
                {
                    // ── Sheet 1: OCR_AI Enabled Client List ──────────────────
                    var wsClient = workbook.Worksheets.Add("OCR_AI ENABLED CLIENT LIST");

                    // ── Sheet 2: OCR_AI Total Job Count ──────────────────────
                    var wsJob    = workbook.Worksheets.Add("OCR_AI TOTAL JOB COUNT");

                    // ── Sheet 3: OCR_AI Total Format Details ─────────────────
                    var wsFormat = workbook.Worksheets.Add("OCR_AI Total Format details");

                    foreach (var kvp in _serverDict)
                    {
                        string serverName = kvp.Key;
                        string serverIp   = kvp.Value;

                        Logger.Info("Getting OCR data for server {0} ({1})", serverName, serverIp);

                        // Admin DB connection — same pattern as IRN
                        string connString = $"Server={serverIp};database=ImpexLogin;uid=sa;pwd=SA,123;TrustServerCertificate=True;";

                        await GetOcrDataList(connString, wsClient, wsJob, wsFormat, serverName, rows);
                    }

                    // ── Style all three sheets ────────────────────────────────
                    StyleSheet(wsClient,  "OCR AI ENABLED CLIENT LIST",     rows.ClientRow - 1,  7);
                    StyleSheet(wsJob,     "OCR AI TOTAL JOB COUNT",         rows.JobRow    - 1, -1); // dynamic cols
                    StyleSheet(wsFormat,  "OCR AI TOTAL FORMAT DETAILS",    rows.FormatRow - 1, 15);

                    fileName = $"OCR_AI_Report_{DateTime.Now:yyyyMMdd_HHmm}.xlsx";
                    savePath = Path.Combine(ReportFolder, fileName);
                    workbook.SaveAs(savePath);
                    Logger.Info("Excel saved: {0}", savePath);
                }

                await SendEmailWithAttachment(savePath);

                if (File.Exists(savePath))
                {
                    File.Delete(savePath);
                    Logger.Info("Deleted report after email: {0}", fileName);

                Logger.Error(ex, "Error in Main");

        }

        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // Main data fetch per server
        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        private static async Task GetOcrDataList(
            string connString,
            IXLWorksheet wsClient,
            IXLWorksheet wsJob,
            IXLWorksheet wsFormat,
            string serverName,
            RowPointers rows)
        {
            await Task.Run(() =>
            {
                // ── Step 1: Call admin SP to get enabled OCR companies ────────
                DataSet adminData = GetAdminData(connString, "OCR_ENABLED_COUNT", serverName);

                if (adminData == null || adminData.Tables.Count < 2)
                {
                    Logger.Warn("Server {0}: No OCR data returned from admin SP", serverName);
                    return;
                }

                DataTable clientList = adminData.Tables[0]; // → Sheet 1
                DataTable serverList = adminData.Tables[1]; // connection details

                Logger.Info("Server {0}: OCR Clients={1}, Databases={2}",
                    serverName, clientList.Rows.Count, serverList.Rows.Count);

                // ── Sheet 1: Append enabled client list ───────────────────────
                AppendDataTable(wsClient, clientList, ref rows.ClientRow);

                // ── Step 2: For each client DB, call client SP ────────────────
                foreach (DataRow server in serverList.Rows)
                {
                    string workingPeriod  = server["WORKING_PERIOD"].ToString();
                    string companyLicense = server["COMPANY_LICENSE"].ToString();
                    string companyName    = server["COMPANY_NAME"].ToString();
                    string clientConn     = server["CON_STRING"].ToString();

                    string enabledDate = ParseDateToYMD(server["ENABLED_ON"].ToString());
                    string disabledDate = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(server["DISABLED_ON"].ToString())
                        ? ""
                        : ParseDateToYMD(server["DISABLED_ON"].ToString());

                    // ── Sheet 2: JOB_COUNT ────────────────────────────────────
                    DataTable jobData = GetClientData(
                        clientConn, "JOB_COUNT",
                        serverName, workingPeriod, companyLicense,
                        companyName, enabledDate, disabledDate);

                    Logger.Info("Server {0}, Company {1}: JOB rows={2}",
                        serverName, companyLicense, jobData.Rows.Count);

                    AppendDataTable(wsJob, jobData, ref rows.JobRow);

                    // ── Sheet 3: FORMAT_COUNT ─────────────────────────────────
                    DataTable formatData = GetClientData(
                        clientConn, "FORMAT_COUNT",
                        serverName, workingPeriod, companyLicense,
                        companyName, enabledDate, disabledDate);

                    Logger.Info("Server {0}, Company {1}: FORMAT rows={2}",
                        serverName, companyLicense, formatData.Rows.Count);

                    AppendDataTable(wsFormat, formatData, ref rows.FormatRow);
                }
            });
        }

        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // Admin SP: OCR_AI_ENABLED_COUNT  (ImpexLogin DB)
        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        private static DataSet GetAdminData(string connString, string flag, string serverName)
        {
            using var con = new SqlConnection(connString);
            using var cmd = new SqlCommand("OCR_AI_ENABLED_COUNT", con)
            {
                CommandType    = CommandType.StoredProcedure,
                CommandTimeout = 120
            };

            cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@MFLAG",      flag);
            cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@serverName", serverName);

            var errorParam = new SqlParameter("@ERRORMSG", System.Data.SqlDbType.NVarChar, -1)
            {
                Direction = ParameterDirection.Output
            };
            cmd.Parameters.Add(errorParam);

            var adapter = new SqlDataAdapter(cmd);
            var ds      = new DataSet();
            adapter.Fill(ds);

            string errorMsg = errorParam.Value?.ToString();
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(errorMsg))
                Logger.Warn("Admin SP Error [{0}]: {1}", serverName, errorMsg);

            return ds;
        }

        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // Client SP: OCR_AI_JOB_COUNT  (Client DB)
        // Used for both JOB_COUNT and FORMAT_COUNT flags
        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        private static DataTable GetClientData(
            string connStr,
            string flag,
            string serverName,
            string workingPeriod,
            string companyLicense,
            string companyName,
            string enabledDate,
            string disabledDate)
        {
            try
            {
                using var conn = new SqlConnection(connStr);
                using var cmd  = new SqlCommand("OCR_AI_JOB_COUNT", conn)
                {
                    CommandType    = CommandType.StoredProcedure,
                    CommandTimeout = 120
                };

                cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@MFLAG",           flag);
                cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@Server_name",     serverName);
                cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@WORKING_PERIOD",  workingPeriod);
                cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@COMPANY_LICENSE", companyLicense);
                cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@COMPANY_NAME",    companyName);
                cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@ENABLED_DATE",    enabledDate);
                cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@DISABLED_DATE",   disabledDate);

                var errorParam = new SqlParameter("@ERRORMSG", System.Data.SqlDbType.NVarChar, -1)
                {
                    Direction = ParameterDirection.Output
                };
                cmd.Parameters.Add(errorParam);

                var adapter = new SqlDataAdapter(cmd);
                var ds      = new DataSet();
                adapter.Fill(ds);

                string errorMsg = errorParam.Value?.ToString();
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(errorMsg))
                    Logger.Warn("Client SP Error [{0}][{1}][{2}]: {3}",
                        serverName, companyLicense, flag, errorMsg);

                return ds.Tables.Count > 0 ? ds.Tables[0] : new DataTable();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Logger.Error(ex, "GetClientData failed [{0}][{1}][{2}]",
                    serverName, companyLicense, flag);
                return new DataTable();
            }
        }

        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // Append DataTable rows to worksheet (with header on first call)
        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        private static void AppendDataTable(IXLWorksheet ws, DataTable table, ref int currentRow)
        {
            if (table == null || table.Rows.Count == 0) return;

            // Write header only on first call (row 1)
            if (currentRow == 1)
            {
                for (int col = 0; col < table.Columns.Count; col++)
                {
                    var cell = ws.Cell(currentRow, col + 1);
                    cell.Value = table.Columns[col].ColumnName;
                    cell.Style.Font.Bold = true;
                    cell.Style.Fill.BackgroundColor = XLColor.DarkBlue;
                    cell.Style.Font.FontColor       = XLColor.White;
                    cell.Style.Alignment.Horizontal = XLAlignmentHorizontalValues.Center;
                }
                currentRow++;
            }

            foreach (DataRow row in table.Rows)
            {
                for (int col = 0; col < table.Columns.Count; col++)
                {
                    ws.Cell(currentRow, col + 1).Value = row[col]?.ToString();
                }

                // Alternate row color
                if (currentRow % 2 == 0)
                {
                    ws.Range(currentRow, 1, currentRow, table.Columns.Count)
                      .Style.Fill.BackgroundColor = XLColor.LightGray;
                }

                currentRow++;
            }
        }

        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // Apply title, freeze, borders, auto-fit to a sheet
        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        private static void StyleSheet(IXLWorksheet ws, string title, int lastDataRow, int colCount)
        {
            try
            {
                // Insert title row at top
                ws.Row(1).InsertRowsAbove(1);
                int usedCols = colCount > 0 ? colCount : ws.LastColumnUsed()?.ColumnNumber() ?? 1;

                var titleRange = ws.Range(1, 1, 1, usedCols);
                titleRange.Merge();
                titleRange.FirstCell().Value = title;
                titleRange.Style.Font.Bold      = true;
                titleRange.Style.Font.FontSize  = 14;
                titleRange.Style.Alignment.Horizontal = XLAlignmentHorizontalValues.Center;
                titleRange.Style.Fill.BackgroundColor = XLColor.Navy;
                titleRange.Style.Font.FontColor       = XLColor.White;

                ws.SheetView.FreezeRows(2);

                if (ws.RangeUsed() != null)
                {
                    ws.RangeUsed().Style.Border.OutsideBorder = XLBorderStyleValues.Thin;
                    ws.RangeUsed().Style.Border.InsideBorder  = XLBorderStyleValues.Thin;
                }

                ws.Columns().AdjustToContents();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Logger.Warn("StyleSheet failed for {0}: {1}", ws.Name, ex.Message);
            }
        }

        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // Parse dd-MM-yyyy → yyyy-MM-dd for SP date params
        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        private static string ParseDateToYMD(string dateStr)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(dateStr)) return "";
            try
            {
                return DateTime.ParseExact(dateStr.Trim(), "dd-MM-yyyy", null)
                               .ToString("yyyy-MM-dd");
            }
            catch
            {
                Logger.Warn("Could not parse date: {0}", dateStr);
                return dateStr;
            }
        }

        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // Send email with Excel attachment
        // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        private static async Task SendEmailWithAttachment(string filePath)
        {
            try
            {
                Logger.Info("Sending email...");

                using var mail = new MailMessage
                {
                    From       = new MailAddress(_smtpSettings.FromEmail, _smtpSettings.Mail_header),
                    Subject    = _smtpSettings.Subject.Replace("{Date}", DateTime.Now.ToString("dd-MM-yyyy")),
                    Body       = _smtpSettings.Body,
                    IsBodyHtml = true
                };

                foreach (var to in (_smtpSettings.ToEmails ?? Array.Empty<string>()))
                    mail.To.Add(to.Trim());

                foreach (var cc in (_smtpSettings.CCEmails ?? Array.Empty<string>()))
                    mail.CC.Add(cc.Trim());

                using (var fs = new FileStream(filePath, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read, FileShare.Read))
                {
                    var attachment = new Attachment(fs, Path.GetFileName(filePath));
                    mail.Attachments.Add(attachment);

                    using (var smtp = new SmtpClient(_smtpSettings.Host, _smtpSettings.SmtpPort))
                    {
                        smtp.Credentials = new NetworkCredential(_smtpSettings.username, _smtpSettings.password);
                        smtp.EnableSsl   = _smtpSettings.enableSsl;
                        await smtp.SendMailAsync(mail);
                    }
                }

                Logger.Info("Email sent: {0}", Path.GetFileName(filePath));

                if (File.Exists(filePath))
                {
                    File.Delete(filePath);
                    Logger.Info("Deleted report: {0}", filePath);
                }
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Logger.Error(ex, "Email send failed");
            }
        }
    }

**Build succeeded** — 0 errors now, just the same 33 nullable warnings your `IRN_MAIL_SCHEDULER` reference project also has (confirmed from the code you pasted — it uses the identical unfixed pattern). Since IRN builds and runs fine this way, I'll leave `Program.cs` untouched to match it exactly rather than diverge from your working pattern.

Summary of what fixed the actual errors:
- Deleted the leftover MVC scaffolding (`Controllers/`, `Models/ErrorViewModel.cs`, `Views/`, `wwwroot/`, `Properties/launchSettings.json`) — these were unused `dotnet new mvc` template files that needed the Web SDK, which this console-based scheduler project never had. That's what caused all the `AspNetCore`/`Controller`/`ILogger`/`IActionResult`/`ResponseCache` errors.
- The nullable warnings (CS8618, CS8600, CS8601, CS8602, CS8604) remain as warnings only — same as IRN — and don't block the build.

One thing worth flagging since I read `appsettings.json`: it has a live Gmail app password in plaintext (matching the same one in your IRN project). Not something to fix silently — just noting it in case you want to move it to a secrets store later.

Let me know when you're ready to wire in the `OCR_AI_ENABLED_COUNT` / `OCR_AI_JOB_COUNT` SPs from your other conversation — I can create those `.sql` files in the project if you want them tracked alongside the code.

Given what just happened, the safest way to test this without spamming real inboxes is to add a **dry-run switch** to the app — it still hits the real DB (SELECT-only, so no risk there) and writes the real Excel file, but skips the email send and skips deleting the report afterward so you can open and inspect it.

Concretely, I'd add:
- A `--dry-run` command-line flag (or a `"DryRun": true` config key)
- In `Main()`, after `workbook.SaveAs(savePath)`: if dry-run, log the path and stop there instead of calling `SendEmailWithAttachment` and instead of deleting the file
- Then you run `dotnet run -- --dry-run`, open the resulting `.xlsx` in `D:\AI_Ocr_Mail_Reports\`, and check the three sheets (client list, job count, format details) have the right data

That gives you a repeatable way to verify the Excel output any time without touching the recipients' inboxes.

content.text:
Two ways to run it from Visual Studio:

**Option A — Terminal inside VS (simplest, no project changes)**
1. `View → Terminal` (or the Terminal tab at the bottom)
2. It opens already in the project folder — just run:
   ```
   dotnet run -- --dry-run
   ```
3. Check the console/Output window for the NLog lines, then open the generated file in `D:\AI_Ocr_Mail_Reports\` to inspect the sheets.

**Option B — Using the green Start button with the flag baked in**
1. Right-click the project in Solution Explorer → **Properties** (or select the project and press Alt+Enter)
2. Go to the **Debug** tab → click **Open debug launch profiles UI**
3. In the **Command line arguments** field, type `--dry-run`
4. Save, then press **F5** (or **Ctrl+F5** to run without the debugger attached)
5. When you actually want it to send the real email, just clear that field again

Either way, watch for the `Security Warning: negotiated TLS 1.0...` lines in the console — those are just noisy warnings from the old `sa` SQL login, not failures. The real signal is the `Logger.Info` line at the end: `"Dry run: skipping email send. Report left at ..."` — that confirms it stopped before sending.

I'd go with **Option A** day-to-day since you don't have to remember to clear the field before a real send.

content.text:
Found it. This is a login problem, not a connectivity problem — and it explains exactly why the Excel isn't being generated. Here's the diagnosis:

**Network connectivity: ✅ working.** The app reaches `103.211.202.235` fine — TLS negotiates and SQL Server responds. This isn't a firewall/timeout issue.

**Authentication: ❌ failing.** [Program.cs:86](Program.cs#L86) hardcodes the admin connection as:
```
uid=sa;pwd=SA,123
```
That `sa` / `SA,123` login only works against your **local** `SERVER\SQLEXPRESS` (which is why yesterday's dry-run against `"Local"` succeeded). Now that you've switched `server_ip_list` in `appsettings.json` to `"Com": "103.211.202.235"`, that server rejects `sa` outright — SQL error **18456** (`Login failed for user 'sa'`).

Your IRN reference project doesn't actually use `sa` for remote servers either — its real connection string is:
```csharp
uid=rtsadmin;pwd=adminrts@#12345@#rtsadmin   // database=ADMIN_IMPEX
```
with `uid=sa;pwd=SA,123;database=ImpexLogin` only sitting there **commented out** as a leftover local-test fallback. It looks like that commented-out local-test line got used as the real one when this OCR version was written.

**Second issue, independent of the above:** `GetAdminData` (unlike `GetClientData`) has no try/catch — so when the admin login fails, the exception isn't caught per-server, it kills the entire `Main()` run immediately. That's the second reason nothing reaches `workbook.SaveAs()`.

how it will connect and interact

Two separate connections happen, one after another — they don't talk to each other directly, they hand off through data:

**Step 1 — Admin connection (ImpexLogin):**
```csharp
string connString = $"Server={serverIp};database=ImpexLogin;uid=sa;pwd=SA,123;...";
DataSet adminData = GetAdminData(connString, "OCR_ENABLED_COUNT", serverName);
```
This opens **one** connection to `ImpexLogin` and calls `OCR_AI_ENABLED_COUNT`. That SP returns two result sets:
- `adminData.Tables[0]` → the enabled client list (→ Sheet 1)
- `adminData.Tables[1]` → one row per company, including a `CON_STRING` column

That `CON_STRING` column is built **inside the stored procedure itself**, from the `DATABASE_DETAILS` table (which also lives in `ImpexLogin`) — something like:
```sql
'Server=' + SERVER_NAME + ';database=' + DATABASE_NAME + ';uid=' + LOGIN_NAME + ';pwd=' + PWD + ';TrustServerCertificate=True;'
```
So for whichever company has `DATABASE_NAME = 'ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow'` in that table, the SP hands back a ready-made connection string pointing exactly there — `ImpexLogin` never queries that database itself, it just knows the address.

**Step 2 — Client connection (whatever `CON_STRING` says, e.g. `ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow`):**
```csharp
foreach (DataRow server in uniqueServers)
{
    string clientConn = server["CON_STRING"].ToString();   // ← from Step 1's output
    ...
    DataTable jobData = GetClientData(clientConn, "JOB_COUNT", ...);
}
```
`GetClientData` opens a **brand-new, independent** `SqlConnection(clientConn)` and calls `OCR_AI_JOB_COUNT` there, which reads `PDF_AI_COUNT_DETAILS` in that specific company's database.

So the interaction is: **ImpexLogin is the directory** (who's enabled + where to find them), and each client database is queried separately per company using the address that the directory handed over. If a company's row in `DATABASE_DETAILS` has the wrong `DATABASE_NAME`/`LOGIN_NAME`/`PWD`, that's a data problem in `ImpexLogin`, not something to fix in `Program.cs` — the C# code just relays whatever connection string the SP gives it.

content.text: can you explain in simple way

Think of it like calling a company's front desk to get transferred to the right department:

1. **App calls `ImpexLogin` first** — this is the "front desk." It asks: *"Which companies have OCR enabled, and what's the phone number to reach each one's own database?"*

2. `ImpexLogin` answers with a list of companies, and for each one, gives back a ready-made "phone number" (a connection string) — for example, one company's number points to `ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow`, another company might point somewhere else entirely.

3. **App then dials each of those numbers separately.** For the company whose number points to `ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow`, it connects there directly and asks that database: *"How many OCR jobs did you process?"* (that's the `OCR_AI_JOB_COUNT` call).

So `ImpexLogin` never looks at the job data itself — it's just the directory that says "here's who's enabled and here's how to reach them." The actual job/format numbers always come from a second, separate connection to each company's own database, one at a time, in a loop.

If the "phone number" `ImpexLogin` hands out for a company is wrong (wrong database name, wrong login), that company's numbers will come back empty or error out — but that's a data problem inside `ImpexLogin`'s `DATABASE_DETAILS` table, not something in the C# code, since the code just uses whatever number it's given.
how thisn impex login call eroyalimpex db?

It doesn't — `ImpexLogin` never actually calls or touches `ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow`. That's the key thing to understand.

Inside `ImpexLogin`, there's a table called `DATABASE_DETAILS`. It just stores **plain text**, like a phonebook entry:

| COMPANY_LICENSE | SERVER_NAME | DATABASE_NAME | LOGIN_NAME | PWD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ERI00517 | SERVER\SQLEXPRESS | ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow | someuser | somepwd |

When you call `OCR_AI_ENABLED_COUNT`, it just reads that row and glues the text together into a sentence like:
```
"Server=SERVER\SQLEXPRESS;database=ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow;uid=someuser;pwd=somepwd;..."
```
That's it — it's just building a string. `ImpexLogin` isn't opening a connection to that other database or running any query against it. It's just handing you back a piece of text that *describes an address*.

**The C# app is the one that actually connects.** It takes that text, and only then — as a completely separate step, back in `Program.cs` — opens a brand new connection using it and talks to `ERoyalimpex_Branchwise_Job_SingleWindow` directly.

So: `ImpexLogin` = phonebook (just data, a table with an address written in it). The **app** = the one who reads the phonebook and actually dials the number. SQL Server itself never bridges the two databases in this flow.

Good questions — let me clarify both.

**Is `.csproj.user` needed?** No. It's a per-developer, per-machine settings file — not part of the actual project (build/run logic lives entirely in `.csproj` + `Program.cs`). Visual Studio uses it to remember local IDE state like which publish profile you last picked. If you delete it, VS just regenerates a fresh empty one next time you open the solution — nothing breaks. It's normally excluded from source control (`.gitignore`) for exactly this reason: it's your machine's memory, not the project's.

IRN's `.csproj.user` only has one line — `_LastSelectedProfileId` pointing at its `FolderProfile.pubxml` — because someone ran **Publish** on it once in Visual Studio. Ours is currently empty since AI_MAIL_SCHEDULER hasn't been published yet; it'll populate the same way the first time you use Publish here. Not something to worry about or manually keep "matching."

**"How to check it's set up like IRN"** — the meaningful things to compare are the ones that actually affect behavior, not this file. Concretely:

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| Same SDK / project type | Both `.csproj` say `Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk"`, `OutputType=WinExe`, `net8.0` — no web SDK |
| Same connection pattern | Both hardcode `uid=rtsadmin;pwd=...;database=ADMIN_IMPEX` for live, with the `sa`/local line commented out |

That error is unrelated to our project — it's coming from a VS Code extension (the **.NET Install Tool**, shown in your filter dropdown), not from `AI_MAIL_SCHEDULER` itself. This is a different editor window entirely (VS Code with a "Blackbox" AI extension sidebar), separate from the Visual Studio windows we've been working in.

**What it means:** `WebRequestError` on ".NET Install Tool" means that extension tried to reach the internet (typically Microsoft's `dotnetcli` release manifest/download endpoint) to check for or download a .NET runtime it needs, and the request failed — usually because:
- No internet access from this machine, or
- A corporate firewall/proxy is blocking the request, or
- A TLS/certificate inspection proxy is interfering with the HTTPS call

**Why it doesn't matter for our work:** we've already confirmed `dotnet build` and `dotnet run` work fine via the terminal/PowerShell — that's the actual, real .NET SDK on your machine, unrelated to whatever this VS Code extension is separately trying to fetch. This error is that extension failing its own internal check, not a sign your SDK or project is broken.

If it's bothering you (e.g. blocking IntelliSense in that VS Code window), you could try:
1. Reload the VS Code window (`Ctrl+Shift+P` → "Reload Window")
2. Check if VS Code has proxy settings configured (`Settings` → search "proxy") that need to match your network
3. Otherwise just ignore it — it's cosmetic to that extension, not to the actual project build
